claim: Vantaca's partner program 'requires an application, intro call, NDA and contract before technical work' (finding 11, summary, and recommendation 7 'its partner track expects a certified integration plus NDA').
problem: The cited page (vantaca.com/become-a-vantaca-partner-vantaca-partner-program) contains no application steps, intro call, NDA or contract requirement. I also fetched vantaca.com/partners in readable and raw modes (253k chars): no occurrence of 'NDA', 'non-disclosure', 'intro', 'kickoff' or 'Apply'. The four-step process cannot be verified on any Vantaca page I could open, yet it is stated as fact and used to justify 'none of these is an entry channel'.
fix: Drop the NDA/intro-call/contract wording, or cite a specific Vantaca URL that prints the steps; otherwise rewrite as inference ('the page positions partners as integrators with technical integration support, so a services-only firm may be gated') and keep the claims to what the page says: dedicated point of contact, technical integration support, structured onboarding, co-marketing.

claim: Summary: 'platform partner programs (Retell, Vapi, Telnyx) are free to join'.
problem: No cited page states a fee of zero. The brief's own resources say 'No fee or minimum published' (Retell), 'Not public' (Vapi, Telnyx). 'Free to join' is an inference presented as fact, and it is inconsistent with the brief's own caveats.
fix: Rephrase to 'no application fee is published for any of the three' or label it as inference.

claim: Finding 3 evidence: 'Retell's own partner blog states services should be "priced separately from usage"' and 'commission, minimum deal sizes and vendor services pricing are questions to agree with the vendor, not assumptions', cited to retellai.com/pricing.
problem: Neither quote appears on the pricing page. The substance does exist in a Retell blog post (retellai.com/blog/voice-ai-partner-deal-scoping, seen in search results), so the claim is true but the citation is wrong.
fix: Cite the blog URL for the quotes and keep the pricing page as the source for the $0.07-$0.31/min figures.

claim: Finding 10: MyCase 'software-integration track is a separate inquiry form'.
problem: The cited consultant-program page describes only the Referral Partner / Certified Consultant / Gold tracks for consultants; no separate software-integration track or inquiry form is mentioned.
fix: Remove the second clause or add the URL where MyCase describes its integration/app partner track.

claim: Finding 7: 'Telnyx announced the program on June 10, 2025 ("now open to select partners"), saying tiered offerings match engagement levels', cited to telnyx.com/partners.
problem: The partner page describes tracks, 'competitive commissions' and 'volume-based rewards' but contains no date, no 'select partners' wording and no tier language. The detail is accurate but lives in the GlobeNewswire release of 10 June 2025 ('The Telnyx Partner Program is now open to select partners'; 'Tiered offerings match varying levels of engagement and capability'), which I opened via rss.globenewswire.com. The release also calls it a 'new Partner Program', not 'Amplify'.
fix: Add the GlobeNewswire release URL as a second source and stop attributing the launch date/tier wording to the partner page.

claim: Finding 12: Applied's partners directory describes 'Preferred consultants for Applied Epic' covering 'workflows, accounting and bookkeeping, IT, security and staffing' and lists Archway Computer and Advantage Microsystems, cited to the press release.
problem: None of that is in the press release. It is, however, on appliedsystems.com/en-us/platform/integrations-partners/ (opened): 'Preferred consultants work with your agency on Applied Epic workflows, accounting and bookkeeping, IT, security and staffing', with Archway Computer ('premier IT support provider ... tailored for independent insurance agencies') and Advantage Microsystems listed.
fix: Cite the integrations-partners directory URL for the consultants claim and keep the release for the certification program.

claim: Recommendation 5: 'duplicate-referral disputes ... which the Promethean analysis identifies as the main way partner economics go wrong'.
problem: Misattributed. Promethean lists attribution among four evaluation checks ('Your agency receives credit for its referrals') and does not call it the main failure mode. The 'most disputes are about attribution' framing comes from the partner.io template page ('Most disputes with referral partners are not about the terms. They are about a referral the partner thinks they sent and you do not remember receiving').
fix: Attribute the dispute point to partner.io and describe Promethean as listing attribution as one of four checks.

claim: Recommendation 4: 'MyCase-certified legal IT consultants and bookkeepers (they already earn 10% of ACV referring MyCase)'.
problem: Slightly misstated. 10% of ACV (annual) / 5% (monthly) is the entry Referral Partner rate; Certified and Gold consultants earn a 'higher'/'highest' unpublished rate, so certified consultants earn more than 10%.
fix: Say 'MyCase referral partners earn 10% of ACV at entry; certified consultants earn a higher unpublished rate'.
